newsitem.title: USA: Clean-up continues at Louisiana pipeline leak.
newsitem.headline: Clean-up continues at Louisiana pipeline leak.

text.p: Efforts to clean thousands of barrels of crude oil from a fragile coast marsh continued Tuesday, and the damaged section of a Texaco pipeline may be repaired by Thursday, authorities said.
"We've recovered 2,555 barrels of oil to date but there's still some out there in pockets and sheens and some slicks," Texaco spokesman Pierre DeGruy told Reuters.
"Repairs are proceeding well, with the damaged section up and analyses underway to determine what happened," he said. "Hopefully, we'll be back in operation Thursday."

The rupture occurred late Friday in Lake Barre in Terrebonne Parish, about 40 miles southwest of New Orleans. The leak created a seven-mile by two-mile slick, with some ribbons of oil intruding into the marshlands on the lake's northern edge and threatening delicate marsh grasses, authorities said.
"It's in the marshes, but a certain amount is evaporating out," DeGruy said.

Louisiana Department of Environmental Quality spokesman Kerry St. Pe said the delicate plants keep that area of the Louisiana marsh intact and they will die if submerged in oily water. Putting boats with booms in the marsh would be as destructive as the oil sheen, he said.
"One of our roles is to guide the cleanup so it isn't more damaging than the oil in a critically eroding area," he said.
State health officials Tuesday closed a number of oyster beds as a precautionary measure and shrimpers and other fishermen also were kept out of the cleanup area.
The 42-mile Texaco pipeline begins at Caillou Island and ends at the Houma, La., station, connecting with the Eugene Island Pipeline System (EIPS), the Coast Guard said.
The 155-mile EIPS, which transports 120,000 barrels of crude oil daily, remained closed as workers tried to repare the Texaco line.
